subject: Streaming chat tail-latency surge during peak concurrency — BrightLane outage
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightlane.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLane Support <support@brightlane.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T08:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming chat — multiple customers seeing long tail latency and reconnects

Hi Rafael,

We're seeing a serious problem since last evening (around 2026-11-11T17:00:00Z) where our users on the BrightLane web app experience long pauses in the streaming chat client. Tokens arrive in bursts, some SSE connections drop and then reconnect, and roughly 12% of sessions report a token delay > 2s (we see spikes up to 8s). This started during our evening peak (EMEA).

We've attached a small HAR and a trace snippet showing repeated 200-but-empty-stream frames and then a large gap. Errors reported on the client look like the stream stalls rather than 5xx responses.

This is hitting our service commitments — can you escalate? We need a short status and ETA for mitigation.

Attachments: har_log_excerpt.txt (text/plain), sse_trace_snippet.json (application/json)

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, BrightLane AI

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightlane.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-12T08:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming chat — multiple customers seeing long tail latency and reconnects

Elena,

Thanks for the report and the artifacts — I see the traces. I'm escalating immediately and standing up a working thread with SRE and the streaming team. We're treating this as high priority.

Immediate asks:
- Can you share the count of concurrent active sessions when you saw the spike?
- Any surfaced errors from your LB (timeouts, connection resets)?

I'll update every 30 minutes until we have a mitigation.

Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-12T09:00:00Z
Subject: [Action required] BrightLane streaming tail-latency surge — diagnostic + customer comms

Team,

BrightLane (key customer, high SLA) is reporting severe tail latency on our hosted streaming chat (SSE/WebSocket) during EMEA peak. They included HAR and trace snippets. Customer impact: retries + degraded UX. They are awaiting an ETA.

Please prioritize:
- Sean: can you correlate this to any infra incidents / autoscaler activity in eu-west-1 between 2026-11-11T16:00Z and 2026-11-12T01:00Z? Check load balancers, ingress egress error rates, and any sudden pod evictions.
- Tessa: grab runtime traces from the streaming runtime (tokenization/kvcache hops) for sessions showing large inter-token gaps. Check kernel selection logs and any fallback to CPU/quantized paths.
- Marissa: prepare a short customer-facing timeline (what we know, immediate mitigations) and confirm whether BrightLane needs a credit or short-term dedicated capacity.

CC Rafael for customer updates. Marking this HIGH.

Thanks,
Rafael

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-12T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: [Action required] BrightLane streaming tail-latency surge — diagnostic + customer comms

Rafael / team,

Initial findings (quick bullet):
- Correlated spike in tail latency (inter-token gaps) across multiple tenant router instances in eu-west-1 starting ~2026-11-11T16:45Z and peaking at 2026-11-11T20:30Z.
- Autoscaler events: a burst of scale-up attempts coincident with the spike; several scale-ups timed out due to slow container startup (image pull delays reported by infra team).
- Ingress layer: elevated keepalive timeouts and 502/504 HTTP proxy timeouts for long-lived SSE streams when backend bundle responded slowly; not full 5xx serving errors but frequent resets.
- No single-model regression observed in perf metrics; the issue looks operational (resource churn + ingress layer pressure) not model-quality.

Immediate mitigation we pushed (in prod):
1) Opened emergency capacity: bumped dedicated burst pool for hosted-api in eu-west-1 by +20% (temporary).
2) Temporarily disabled the new routing optimization that reduced connection affinity — rolling back that change seems to reduce stream churn.
3) Short-term ingress timeout tuning: extended keepalive and proxy read timeout for SSE routes by 10s to reduce premature resets while we stabilize.

Related artifacts: PagerDuty incident PD-98765, Jira SUP-1234.

Next: Tessa to confirm whether the runtime saw increased kernel latency (KV cache thrashing / compaction) and to provide logs for sessions flagged by BrightLane trace. Marissa pls send the customer note once we've agreed text.

-Sean
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-12T10:10:00Z
Subject: Re: [Action required] BrightLane streaming tail-latency surge — diagnostic + customer comms

Folks,

Log excerpts (sanitized):
- 2026-11-11T18:12:45Z stream_session_id=uh3k token_emit_gap=5387ms kernel_exec_ms=42 kv_cache_miss=0
- 2026-11-11T18:12:50Z stream_session_id=uh3k token_emit_gap=6123ms kernel_exec_ms=44 kv_cache_miss=1
- 2026-11-11T19:03:12Z new_conn_backoff=1.2s image_pull_delay=72s (infra)

Observations:
- Kernel exec time per token is normal; the large gap is between kernel runs suggesting scheduling/backpressure at the runtime dispatcher or network layer.
- We see evidence of KV-cache compaction and occasional GC pauses on a small subset of nodes that were under sustained high connection counts.

Mitigations applied / recommended:
- Forced traffic away from affected nodes (drain + reprovision) — improves per-token spacing in canary tests.
- Increased per-node connection ceiling and enabled aggressive batching (shorter batch windows) to avoid bursty dispatch; this helps latency at moderate cost increase.
- Recommend keeping the routing affinity rollback and increasing temporary capacity until the infra image pull issue is resolved.

I'll attach the raw snippet from the runtime (sse_trace_snippet.json) for the team. If these mitigations hold, we can provide BrightLane an ETA for full remediation in ~3 hours and follow-up with capacity/patch schedule.

-Tessa
Staff Software Engineer, Streaming Runtime

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightlane.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-12T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming chat — multiple customers seeing long tail latency and reconnects

Elena,

Quick update and next steps (TL;DR — temporary mitigations in place; target full remediation in ~3 hours):

What we found:
- The issue was operational: a combination of image-pull delays that slowed autoscaler scale-ups in eu-west-1 plus a routing optimization we recently enabled that reduced connection affinity. These caused connection churn and backend node pressure, which produced long inter-token gaps for streaming clients.

What we did (already applied):
- Rolled back the routing optimization for SSE/WebSocket routes (reduced churn).
- Opened emergency burst capacity in eu-west-1 (+20%) to absorb peak traffic.
- Increased ingress keepalive/proxy read timeouts to reduce premature client resets.
- Drained and reprovisioned a handful of nodes showing KV-cache compaction/GC pauses.

Next steps and ETA:
- Monitoring closely; if we remain stable over the next 3 hours we'll remove the emergency capacity. We'll follow up with a post-incident note that includes timeline and long-term fixes (image pull improvements, routing policy tweaks, and autoscaler hardening).

We appreciate the traces you sent — they helped narrow the root cause quickly. I'll send a customer-facing timeline in ~30m and follow up when we have final confirmation. If you see another spike, please flag immediately and we'll escalate to execs.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Lead — Redwood Inference
